docs.title: CTSM on HiPerGator
docs.text: Documentation for running the Community Terrestrial Systems Model (CTSM) on HiPerGator at the University of Florida.

docs.title: What is CTSM?
docs.text:
CTSM is the land component of the Community Earth System Model (CESM). It simulates terrestrial ecosystem processes including:

  • Vegetation dynamics and carbon cycling
  • Hydrology and water balance
  • Energy balance and heat transfer
  • Biogeochemistry (carbon-nitrogen cycling)

CTSM can be run standalone (without ocean/atmosphere coupling) for land-focused research.

docs.title: Glossary
docs.text: Key terms for CTSM development on HiPerGator.

docs.title: Models & Components
docs.text:
CTSM - Community Terrestrial Systems Model. The land model, designed to run standalone or as part of CESM. GitHub

CESM - Community Earth System Model. Fully-coupled global climate model. CTSM is its land component.

CLM - Community Land Model. The land component within CTSM that models vegetation, hydrology, carbon cycling, etc.

CIME - Common Infrastructure for Modeling the Earth (pronounced "SEAM"). Provides the case control system for configuring, building, and running Earth system models.

FATES - Functionally Assembled Terrestrial Ecosystem Simulator. A vegetation demographic model that can be coupled to CLM for more detailed vegetation dynamics. FATES GitHub

docs.title: Tools & Utilities
docs.text:
cprnc - Tool for comparing NetCDF files. Used to verify model output. Each group builds their own (see Prerequisites).

git-fleximod - CTSM's tool for managing submodules. Replaces the older manage_externals used by CESM.

mksurfdata - Tool for generating surface datasets (fsurdat files) for CTSM. Requires PIO library.

PIO (ParallelIO) - Parallel I/O library required for mksurfdata. Each group builds their own (see Prerequisites).

docs.title: Configuration & Data
docs.text:
CLM_USRDAT - Resolution setting for user-provided datasets. Used with subset data for single-point runs.

Compset - Component set. A predefined combination of model components and configurations. Each compset has a short alias and a long name of the form TIME_ATM_LND_ICE_OCN_ROF_GLC_WAV[_BGC], where each component may carry a % modifier. Example: the alias I1850Clm60BgcCrop has the long name 1850_DATM%GSWP3v1_CLM60%BGC-CROP_SICE_SOCN_MOSART_SGLC_SWAV (pre-industrial 1850, data atmosphere, CLM 6.0 with BGC and crops).

Namelist - Fortran configuration file format. Key files: user_nl_clm, user_nl_datm_streams.

PFT - Plant Functional Type. Categories of vegetation (e.g., broadleaf deciduous tree, C3 grass, corn) that share similar characteristics. CTSM uses PFTs to represent vegetation at each grid point.

Surface data (fsurdat) - NetCDF file containing land surface characteristics (soil, vegetation, topography).

docs.title: Output Files
docs.text:
History files - Model output files containing time-varying data (.clm2.h0a.*.nc, .clm2.h1a.*.nc, etc.; since ctsm5.3.062 averaged and instantaneous fields go to separate hXa and hXi files). Configured via hist_* namelist variables. Use for analysis and plotting.

Restart files - Checkpoint files (.r.nc) that capture the complete model state. Used to continue simulations from a specific point. Required for branch runs and spinup continuation.

docs.title: Case Directories
docs.text:
CASEROOT - Case configuration directory. Contains XML settings, namelists, scripts.

EXEROOT - Build directory where compiled code lives.

RUNDIR - Runtime directory containing output, restarts, logs.

DOUT_S_ROOT - Archive directory for completed output.

docs.title: Run Types
docs.text:
startup - Fresh start with cold initialization.

branch - Exact continuation from a restart file. Preserves bit-for-bit answers.

hybrid - New start initialized from another case's restart file. Allows configuration changes.

docs.title: Spinup
docs.text:
AD spinup - Accelerated Decomposition spinup. First phase (~200 years is the NCAR guideline; site runs may differ) with accelerated soil carbon turnover.

Post-AD spinup - Second phase (several hundred years) with normal turnover rates to reach equilibrium.

docs.title: Infrastructure
docs.text:
ccs_config - Repository containing machine configurations for CIME. Our fork adds HiPerGator support.

ESMF - Earth System Modeling Framework. Provides coupling infrastructure.

NUOPC - National Unified Operational Prediction Capability. Layer built on ESMF for coupling standards.

SCRIP - Spherical Coordinate Remapping and Interpolation Package. Used for creating mapping files.

docs.title: HiPerGator Specific
docs.text:
HPG - HiPerGator. UF's supercomputer.

lmod - Module system for managing software environments.

SLURM - Job scheduler for submitting work to compute nodes.

QOS - Quality of Service. Defines resource limits for job queues.

docs.title: Hillslope and OSBS Project Terms
docs.text:
Terms used in the Swenson Implementation and Research pages.

A_thresh - Flow-accumulation threshold (in pixels) above which a cell is treated as stream. Set to int(0.5 × Lc²); 63,362 pixels for OSBS.

Chain index - A hillslope column's 1-based position in the downhill chain (column_index). In the OSBS file, index 1 is the lake column (terminal, drains out of the hillslope), indices 2-25 are land Bins 1-24, and each column drains to the one below it.

CDEPS - Community Data models for Earth Prediction Systems. The NUOPC-based data components (including DATM) and their stream-reading code.

DATM - Data atmosphere component. Reads prescribed atmospheric forcing (e.g., CRUNCEP, NEON tower data) from stream files instead of running an atmosphere model.

DTND - Distance To Nearest Drainage. Straight-line horizontal distance from a pixel to the stream or open-water cell it drains to.

FZ - Flood zone. The 12 OSBS hillslope bins with raw HAND below 0 (below the level of the drainage cell); the other 12 are upland bins.

HAND - Height Above Nearest Drainage. Elevation of a pixel relative to the stream or open-water cell it drains to. Conditioned HAND is computed on the pit-filled, flat-resolved DEM and is ≥ 0. Raw HAND subtracts the depression-fill depth, so it is negative inside filled depressions.

Lc - Characteristic length scale of the terrain, from the peak of the Laplacian-of-elevation spectrum. 356 m (355.98 m) for the OSBS production domain.

MERIT - MERIT DEM, a ~90 m global elevation model. Swenson & Lawrence (2025) built the global hillslope dataset from it; this project reproduces that dataset to verify the pipeline.

NWI - National Wetlands Inventory (US Fish & Wildlife Service). Source of the OSBS open-water mask used for the lake column.

O_SCALAR - CTSM history field: the fraction by which soil decomposition is reduced due to anoxia (1 = no reduction). Only active when use_lch4 = .true..

OSBS - Ordway-Swisher Biological Station, the NEON site in north-central Florida used as the test site.

Phase (A-I) - Work phases of the OSBS hillslope project, recorded in swenson/phases/ in hpg-esm-tools. Phase H Track A is the single-cell mesh workaround for CTSM Issue #1432 (see Lateral Flow and Routing).

Q01 / Q99 - 1st and 99th percentiles of raw HAND over the domain (-6.35 m and +17.02 m in production). Pixels outside this range are discarded before binning.

R4C5-R12C14 - The production domain: NEON 1 km DTM tile rows 4-12 and columns 5-14 (90 tiles, 9 × 10 km, no missing data).

SourceMod - A modified copy of a CTSM source file placed in a case's SourceMods/src.clm/, compiled in place of the original for that case only.

TAI - Terrestrial-aquatic interface. The shifting boundary between wet and dry ground in low-relief wetland landscapes; the project's central scientific target.

docs.title: Onboarding
docs.text: This page provides essential HiPerGator information for running CTSM. For comprehensive Linux training, see the resources at the bottom.

docs.title: HiPerGator Basics
docs.text: HiPerGator is UF's supercomputer - a cluster of connected nodes that share resources. You interact with it via the command line.

docs.title: Key Concepts
docs.text: Concept Description Login nodes Where you land when you SSH in. For light tasks only (editing, file management) Compute nodes Where jobs run. Access via SLURM scheduler SLURM Job scheduler - submits work to compute nodes lmod Module system for loading software (compilers, libraries)

docs.title: Storage Locations
docs.text:
Path Purpose Notes /home/$USER/ Config files, small files 40GB quota, not backed up; daily and weekly snapshots in ~/.snapshot /blue/<group>/$USER/ Active projects, code, data Group allocation, Lustre parallel filesystem, not backed up /orange/<group>/ Archival storage Slow - don't use for active work

Replace <group> with your research group's allocation (e.g., gerber, biology, etc.).

docs.title: Module Environment
docs.text:
CTSM requires specific modules. We use a saved module collection:

# Load the CTSM module collection
module restore ctsm-modules

# Verify modules are loaded
module list

The collection includes: GCC 14.2.0, OpenMPI 5.0.7, NetCDF, HDF5, ESMF 8.8.1, CMake, Python 3.12

docs.title: Recommended Shortcuts
docs.text:
These environment variables can save typing. Add them to your ~/.bashrc and customize for your setup:

# Your workspace (customize <group>)
export BLUE="/blue/<group>/$USER"
export CASES="$BLUE/cases"

# Your CTSM installation (after cloning)
export CTSMROOT="$BLUE/ctsm5.3"
export CIME_SCRIPTS="$CTSMROOT/cime/scripts"

# Your group's input data location
export INPUT_DATA="/blue/<group>/earth_models/inputdata"

# Shared single-point subset data (used on the Running CTSM pages)
export SUBSET_DATA="/blue/<group>/earth_models/shared.subset.data"

# Analysis scripts and the pysheds fork (used on the hillslope pages)
export TOOLS="$BLUE/hpg-esm-tools"
export PYSHEDS_FORK="$BLUE/pysheds_fork"
alias pysheds-env='export PYTHONPATH="$PYSHEDS_FORK:$PYTHONPATH"'

After editing, reload: source ~/.bashrc

Tip

The exact paths depend on where you install CTSM and where your group stores input data. These are suggestions, not requirements.

docs.title: SLURM Basics
docs.text:
Submit jobs to compute nodes - never run heavy computation on login nodes.

# Check your running jobs
squeue -u $USER

# Check group jobs (replace <group>)
squeue -A <group>

# Cancel a job
scancel <job_id>

# View job details
scontrol show job <job_id>

docs.title: Group QOS Limits
docs.text:
Each group has its own resource limits. Check your group's QoS:

showQos <group>

This shows your group's CPU, memory, and GPU limits. CTSM cases will fail if they request more resources than your QoS allows.

docs.title: CIME Configuration
docs.text: CTSM uses CIME (Common Infrastructure for Modeling the Earth) for building and running cases. This page explains the HiPerGator-specific configuration and what you may need to customize.

docs.title: How CIME Finds Machine Config
docs.text:
CIME looks for machine configurations in this order:

  1. ~/.cime/ (user overrides)
  2. $CTSMROOT/ccs_config/machines/<machine>/ (machine-specific)
  3. $CTSMROOT/ccs_config/machines/ (defaults)

Our fork includes HiPerGator configs at: 

ccs_config/machines/hipergator/
├── config_machines.xml    # Machine definition
├── config_batch.xml       # SLURM settings
└── gnu_hipergator.cmake   # Compiler flags

docs.title: config_machines.xml
docs.text: The main machine definition. Key sections:

docs.title: Basic System Info
docs.text:
<DESC>UF HiPerGator | hpg-default node | AMD ROME 128 cores per node | slurm</DESC>
<OS>LINUX</OS>
<COMPILERS>gnu</COMPILERS>
<MPILIBS>openmpi</MPILIBS>

docs.title: File Paths
docs.text:
These define where CTSM reads/writes data:

<CIME_OUTPUT_ROOT>/blue/gerber/$ENV{USER}/earth_model_output/cime_output_root</CIME_OUTPUT_ROOT>
<DIN_LOC_ROOT>/blue/gerber/earth_models/inputdata</DIN_LOC_ROOT>
<DOUT_S_ROOT>$CIME_OUTPUT_ROOT/archive/$CASE</DOUT_S_ROOT>
Variable Purpose CIME_OUTPUT_ROOT Where case build/run directories are created DIN_LOC_ROOT Where CTSM looks for (and downloads) input data DOUT_S_ROOT Where output is archived after runs complete

You Must Customize These

Change /blue/gerber/ to your group's allocation path.

docs.title: Node Configuration
docs.text:
<MAX_TASKS_PER_NODE>128</MAX_TASKS_PER_NODE>
<MAX_MPITASKS_PER_NODE>128</MAX_MPITASKS_PER_NODE>

HiPerGator's default nodes have 128 cores. This tells CIME how to distribute MPI tasks.

docs.title: Module System
docs.text:
The config tells CIME which modules to load:

<modules>
  <command name="load">cmake/3.26.4</command>
  <command name="load">gcc/14.2.0</command>
  <command name="load">openmpi/5.0.7</command>
  <!-- ... more modules ... -->
</modules>

These must match your ctsm-modules collection.

docs.title: Environment Variables
docs.text:
<environment_variables>
  <env name="NETCDF_PATH">$ENV{HPC_NETCDF_C_DIR}</env>
  <env name="PIO">/blue/gerber/earth_models/shared/parallelio/bld</env>
  <!-- ... more variables ... -->
</environment_variables>

PIO Path

The PIO paths point to the shared ParallelIO build. Update these to your group's build location.

docs.title: PIO Shared Library
docs.text:
Our fork includes configuration to use a pre-built PIO library instead of rebuilding it for every case. This is controlled by three environment variables:

<environment_variables>
  <!-- Basic PIO paths -->
  <env name="PIO">/blue/<group>/earth_models/shared/parallelio/bld</env>
  <env name="PIO_LIBDIR">/blue/<group>/earth_models/shared/parallelio/bld/lib</env>
  <env name="PIO_INCDIR">/blue/<group>/earth_models/shared/parallelio/bld/include</env>

  <!-- These tell case.build to use external PIO -->
  <env name="PIO_VERSION_MAJOR">2</env>
  <env name="PIO_TYPENAME_VALID_VALUES">netcdf</env>
  <env name="LD_LIBRARY_PATH">/blue/<group>/earth_models/shared/parallelio/bld/lib:$ENV{LD_LIBRARY_PATH}</env>
</environment_variables>
Variable Purpose PIO_VERSION_MAJOR Tells CIME to use external PIO (must match your PIO version) PIO_TYPENAME_VALID_VALUES Specifies supported I/O backends (netcdf for our build) LD_LIBRARY_PATH Required for runtime dynamic linking to .so files

How it works: During case.build, CIME checks if PIO_VERSION_MAJOR is set. If it matches the expected version, CIME uses your external PIO library instead of building one. You'll see "Using installed PIO library" in the build log.

Build Time Savings

Without these settings, every case.build compiles PIO from source, adding several minutes to each build. With external PIO, builds are noticeably faster.

docs.title: config_batch.xml
docs.text:
SLURM job submission settings:

<batch_system MACH="hipergator" type="slurm">
  <batch_submit>sbatch</batch_submit>
  <submit_args>
    <arg flag="--time" name="$JOB_WALLCLOCK_TIME"/>
    <arg flag="-q" name="$JOB_QUEUE"/>
    <arg flag="--mem" name="16GB"/>
  </submit_args>
  <directives>
    <directive>--partition=hpg-default</directive>
    <directive>--mail-type=NONE</directive>
  </directives>
  <queues>
    <queue jobmin="1" jobmax="20" default="true">gerber</queue>
    <queue jobmin="1" jobmax="128">gerber-b</queue>
  </queues>
</batch_system>

docs.title: Key Settings
docs.text:
No --exclusive flag: Unlike many HPC centers, HiPerGator shares nodes by default. We don't include --exclusive because: - Most CTSM runs use few cores - Exclusive access wastes resources - QoS limits often don't allow full-node jobs anyway

Memory request: Fixed at 16GB. Adjust if your runs need more.

Queues section:

You Must Change This

The queue names (gerber, gerber-b) are QoS names specific to the Gerber group. Replace these with your group's QoS names.

Check your group's QoS: 

showQos <your_group>

The jobmin and jobmax values limit task counts for each queue.

docs.title: gnu_hipergator.cmake
docs.text:
Compiler flags and library linking:

# NetCDF legacy macro support
string(APPEND CPPDEFS " -DNETCDF_ENABLE_LEGACY_MACROS")

# Link netcdf and lapack
string(APPEND SLIBS " ${SHELL_CMD_OUTPUT_BUILD_INTERNAL_IGNORE0}")
string(APPEND SLIBS " -L$(LAPACK_LIBDIR) -llapack -lblas")

# Lustre filesystem optimization
set(PIO_FILESYSTEM_HINTS "lustre")

You probably won't need to modify this file.

docs.title: Required Changes
docs.text:
1. File paths in config_machines.xml:
  2. CIME_OUTPUT_ROOT: Change /blue/gerber/ to /blue/<your_group>/
  3. DIN_LOC_ROOT: Point to your group's inputdata location

  4. PIO paths: Point to your group's ParallelIO build

  5. Queue names in config_batch.xml:

  6. Replace gerber and gerber-b with your group's QoS names

docs.title: Optional Changes
docs.text:
• Memory: Increase --mem in config_batch.xml if needed
  • Email: Change mail settings in config_batch.xml
  • Partition: Change from hpg-default if using GPU nodes

docs.title: Making Changes
docs.text:
After modifying config files:

# If you already have cases built, they may need rebuilding
cd /path/to/your/case
./case.build --clean-all
./case.build

New cases will automatically use the updated configs.

docs.title: The ~/.cime Alternative
docs.text:
CIME supports user-level config overrides in ~/.cime/. You could theoretically:

  1. Clone upstream CTSM (no fork needed)
  2. Put HiPerGator configs in ~/.cime/

Why we don't recommend this:

  • Batch config loading has bugs in CIME v3
  • NODENAME_REGEX machine detection is unreliable
  • Each user must maintain their own configs
  • Harder to share and troubleshoot

The fork approach gives everyone consistent, working configs.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
"Machine not found" : Check that ccs_config/machines/hipergator/ exists and submodules are initialized

Job submission fails : Verify queue names match your group's QoS

Build can't find libraries : Check that module versions in config match your ctsm-modules collection

Wrong output location : Check CIME_OUTPUT_ROOT path in config_machines.xml

docs.title: Fork Reference
docs.text: This page explains why and how we forked CTSM for HiPerGator. Use this as a reference for understanding our modifications or for creating your own fork.

docs.title: Why We Fork
docs.text: CTSM isn't plug-and-play on HiPerGator. Several issues require source-level modifications.

docs.title: 1. Machine Configuration (ccs_config)
docs.text:
CTSM uses CIME (Common Infrastructure for Modeling the Earth) for builds and job submission. CIME needs machine-specific configuration files that define:

  • Compiler paths and flags
  • MPI library settings
  • SLURM batch directives
  • Input data locations

HiPerGator isn't in the upstream machine list, so we need custom configs.

The complication: Machine configs live in a separate repository (ccs_config_cesm) that CTSM pulls in as a git submodule. To add HiPerGator support, we had to:

  1. Fork ccs_config_cesm
  2. Add HiPerGator configs to our fork
  3. Fork CTSM to point its .gitmodules at our ccs_config fork

This submodule-of-a-submodule situation makes the fork necessary.

docs.title: 2. User Config (~/.cime) Doesn't Work Reliably
docs.text:
CIME v3 theoretically supports user config overrides in ~/.cime/. We tried this approach and encountered bugs:

  • Batch configuration loading was inconsistent
  • NODENAME_REGEX machine detection failed intermittently
  • Each user had to maintain their own config files

Forking ccs_config gives us a single source of truth that works reliably for everyone.

docs.title: 3. Build Tool Bugs
docs.text:
Several CTSM build tools have issues with newer GCC versions:

Issue Symptom Fix PIO linking mksurfdata fails to link Change STATIC to SHARED in CMakeLists.txt Format specifiers gfortran compilation errors Explicit widths in Fortran format specs (I → I0 for writes, (i) → (I6) for the read) GCC compatibility flags gfortran errors on argument mismatches and BOZ literals (GCC 10+) Add -fallow-argument-mismatch and -fallow-invalid-boz to the mksurfdata build

The PIO linking and format-specifier fixes were merged upstream (#3700 in ctsm5.4.021, #3701 in ctsm5.4.025). The ctsm5.3.x tags our fork is based on still need them. The GCC flags remain fork-only. See Fork Modifications.

docs.title: 4. HiPerGator-Specific Paths
docs.text: Default paths in some tools point to NCAR systems. Our fork updates paths to work with HiPerGator's storage layout.

docs.title: Repository Structure
docs.text:
Repository Branch Purpose cdevaneprugh/CTSM uf-ctsm5.3.085 CTSM with tool fixes cdevaneprugh/ccs_config_cesm uf-hipergator Machine configuration cdevaneprugh/NCAR-NEON uf-osbs NEON→DATM forcing generator (offline fork; AGPL-3.0)

The ccs_config fork is included as a submodule of the CTSM fork.

The NCAR-NEON fork is separate from the CTSM/ccs_config build forks: it is the NEON atmospheric-forcing generator, modified to run offline on HiPerGator, and is used to produce input data, not to build the model. It is documented at NEON Atmospheric Forcing; the "Using This Fork" and "Updating the Fork" sections below concern the CTSM fork only.

Version Notice

These forks are based on CTSM 5.3.085. Other versions may have different issues or may have fixed some of these bugs upstream.

docs.title: CTSM Modifications
docs.text: File Change Reason tools/mksurfdata_esmf/src/CMakeLists.txt STATIC → SHARED Fix for shared PIO libraries tools/mksurfdata_esmf/src/mksurfdata.F90 Format specifiers I → I0 (writes), (i) → (I6) (read) gfortran requires explicit widths tools/mksurfdata_esmf/gen_mksurfdata_build Added GCC compatibility flags Compatibility workarounds python/ctsm/site_and_regional/single_point_case.py MPILIB=openmpi HiPerGator uses OpenMPI tools/site_and_regional/default_data_*.cfg Input paths HiPerGator data locations

docs.title: ccs_config Modifications
docs.text:
The machines/hipergator/ directory contains:

  • config_machines.xml - Full machine definition (compilers, paths, MPI settings)
  • config_batch.xml - SLURM batch settings (no --exclusive flag for shared nodes)
  • gnu_hipergator.cmake - Compiler flags and library paths

See CIME Configuration for detailed explanation of these files.

docs.title: Option 1: Clone Directly
docs.text:
The simplest approach - clone our fork and use it as-is. See Quick Start for installation steps.

You'll need to customize the QoS settings in the config files for your group (see CIME Configuration).

docs.title: Option 2: Fork from Us
docs.text:
If you need additional modifications:

  1. Fork cdevaneprugh/CTSM on GitHub
  2. Clone your fork
  3. Make your modifications
  4. Update the ccs_config submodule if needed

This gives you a customizable base with our fixes already applied.

docs.title: Option 3: Start from Upstream
docs.text:
If you need a different CTSM version or want full control:

  1. Fork ESCOMP/CTSM on GitHub
  2. Fork ESMCI/ccs_config_cesm
  3. Apply the modifications listed above
  4. Update .gitmodules to point to your ccs_config fork

This is more work but gives you a clean slate.

docs.title: Updating the Fork
docs.text:
When upstream releases a new CTSM version:

# Add upstream remote (one time)
git remote add upstream https://github.com/ESCOMP/CTSM.git

# Fetch new tags
git fetch upstream --tags

# Create new branch from new tag (replace <new-tag>, e.g. a ctsm5.4.x tag)
git checkout -b uf-<new-tag> <new-tag>

# Cherry-pick modifications from old branch
git cherry-pick <commit-hash>...

# Update submodules
./bin/git-fleximod update

# Test and push
git push -u origin uf-<new-tag>

Check if fixes are still needed

Before cherry-picking, check if upstream has fixed the issues. The PIO linking and format-specifier fixes are already upstream from ctsm5.4.025 onward, so those two do not need to be carried forward.

docs.title: Building mksurfdata
docs.text: The mksurfdata tool generates surface datasets (fsurdat files) for CTSM. This page covers building the tool on HiPerGator.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
Before building mksurfdata, ensure you have:

  1. Module collection loaded: module restore ctsm-modules
  2. PIO library built and path set (see Prerequisites)
  3. CTSM fork cloned (fixes are already applied)

docs.title: Building the Executable
docs.text:
# Load modules
module restore ctsm-modules

# Set PIO path (customize for your group)
export PIO="/blue/<group>/earth_models/shared/parallelio/bld"

# Navigate to mksurfdata directory
cd $CTSMROOT/tools/mksurfdata_esmf

# Build for HiPerGator
./gen_mksurfdata_build --machine hipergator

Expected output: 

Successfully created mksurfdata_esmf executable for: hipergator_gnu for openmpi library

docs.title: Verify the Build
docs.text:
Check that PIO libraries are properly linked:

cd tool_bld
ldd mksurfdata | grep libpio

Each research group should set up a directory structure for CTSM resources. Here's a recommended layout:

docs.title: Why Modules (Not Conda)
docs.text: If you're familiar with conda, you might wonder if you can manage CTSM dependencies that way instead of using lmod. Here's why we use system modules for CTSM builds.

docs.title: HPC Build Dependencies Need System Tools
docs.text: Aspect Conda lmod (System Modules) MPI/SLURM integration Problematic (PMIx often missing) Native support, cluster-tuned Compiler optimization Generic builds Tuned for node hardware Library compatibility May conflict with system libs Configured by HPC admins ESMF availability Exists but may not match MPI Built for cluster's MPI Best for Python packages, dev tools Compiled HPC dependencies

docs.title: ESMF Requires Real MPI
docs.text:
Modern CTSM (5.3+) uses CDEPS (data models) and CMEPS (the NUOPC mediator) for atmospheric data coupling. These components require ESMF (Earth System Modeling Framework), which in turn requires a real MPI implementation.

On HiPerGator, ESMF is built with OpenMPI and configured for SLURM. Conda's MPI packages often lack:

  • PMIx support - Required for SLURM job launch
  • Cluster fabric optimization - InfiniBand tuning, NUMA awareness
  • Consistent ABI - May conflict with system libraries

Result: Even single-point runs that use only 1 MPI task still require OpenMPI because of ESMF.

Why not mpi-serial?

CIME supports mpi-serial for truly serial execution, but it doesn't work with modern CTSM. The ESMF library links against OpenMPI symbols that mpi-serial can't provide. See Fork Modifications for details.

docs.title: When Conda Is Appropriate
docs.text:
Conda works well for:

  • Python analysis packages - xarray, matplotlib, pandas for post-processing
  • Development tools - Editors, linters, formatters
  • CTSM Python tools - The ctsm_pylib environment for subset_data and other scripts

We use a hybrid approach:

  • lmod modules for compiled dependencies (compilers, MPI, NetCDF, ESMF)
  • conda environments for Python-only tools and analysis

This gives you the reliability of system-optimized builds with the flexibility of conda for scripting.

docs.title: Shared Libraries
docs.text: These libraries need to be built once per group and can be shared among group members.

docs.title: cprnc (NetCDF Comparison Tool)
docs.text: Used to compare NetCDF output files. Useful for validating model output.

docs.title: ParallelIO (PIO)
docs.text:
PIO (Parallel I/O) is a library that provides a high-level interface to NetCDF and other I/O formats. CTSM uses PIO for:

  • mksurfdata_esmf - The tool that generates surface datasets
  • CTSM runtime - Reading input data and writing history output

Why Build PIO Separately?

CTSM can build PIO automatically during case.build, but this rebuilds it for every new case. Building PIO once as a shared library saves significant time. With proper configuration (see CIME Configuration), CTSM uses your pre-built PIO instead of rebuilding.

Shared Libraries Required

PIO must be built with BUILD_SHARED_LIBS=ON for mksurfdata to work correctly. The upstream CMakeLists.txt has a bug that declares libraries as STATIC but expects shared .so files. See Fork Modifications for details.

Set the PIO environment variable to point to your build:

export PIO="/blue/<group>/earth_models/shared/parallelio/bld"

docs.title: Building Shared Libraries
docs.text: Build these once for your group. Each group member can then use the same installation.

docs.title: Building cprnc
docs.text:
module restore ctsm-modules

git clone https://github.com/ESMCI/cprnc.git
cd cprnc
mkdir bld && cd bld
cmake ../
make

docs.title: Building PIO
docs.text:
module restore ctsm-modules

git clone https://github.com/NCAR/ParallelIO.git parallelio
cd parallelio

# In-source configure: run from parallelio/, install into parallelio/bld
cmake \
  -DNetCDF_C_PATH=/apps/gcc/14.2.0/openmpi/5.0.7/netcdf-c/4.9.3 \
  -DNetCDF_Fortran_PATH=/apps/gcc/14.2.0/openmpi/5.0.7/netcdf-f/4.6.2 \
  -DWITH_PNETCDF=OFF \
  -DBUILD_SHARED_LIBS=ON \
  -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=`pwd`/bld \
  -DCMAKE_INSTALL_RPATH=`pwd`/src/gptl \
  -DCMAKE_INSTALL_RPATH_USE_LINK_PATH=TRUE \
  .

make
make install

Key CMake flags:

Flag Purpose BUILD_SHARED_LIBS=ON Required - Creates .so files instead of .a WITH_PNETCDF=OFF Skip parallel-netcdf (not needed for CTSM) CMAKE_INSTALL_RPATH Ensures runtime library paths are embedded

ls bld/lib/*.so
# Should show: libgptl.so libpioc.so libpiof.so

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text: Get CTSM running on HiPerGator. This guide covers the minimum steps to clone, build, and run your first case.

docs.title: Before You Begin
docs.text:
You'll need:

  • HiPerGator account with group allocation on /blue/
  • Basic familiarity with the Linux command line
  • ~50GB free space for CTSM installation (input data is separate)

New to HiPerGator? See Onboarding first.

docs.title: Step 1: Set Up Modules
docs.text:
CTSM requires specific compiler and library versions. Create a module collection:

module purge

# Load required modules
module load subversion/1.9.7
module load perl/5.24.1
module load cmake/3.26.4
module load python/3.12
module load gcc/14.2.0
module load lapack/3.11.0
module load openmpi/5.0.7
module load netcdf-c/4.9.3 netcdf-f/4.6.2
module load hdf5
module load esmf/8.8.1

# Save the collection for future sessions
module save ctsm-modules

From now on, just run module restore ctsm-modules to load all modules.

docs.title: Step 2: Clone CTSM
docs.text:
We maintain a fork with HiPerGator-specific fixes. Clone it:

cd /blue/<group>/$USER

# Clone from our fork
git clone https://github.com/cdevaneprugh/CTSM.git ctsm5.3
cd ctsm5.3

# Checkout the HiPerGator branch
git checkout uf-ctsm5.3.085

Replace <group> with your research group's allocation name.

docs.title: Step 3: Initialize Submodules
docs.text:
CTSM uses git-fleximod to manage submodules (including the machine configuration):

./bin/git-fleximod update

This downloads all required components. It may take a few minutes.

docs.title: Step 4: Verify Installation
docs.text:
Check that everything is in place:

# Check submodule status
./bin/git-fleximod status

# Verify HiPerGator config exists
ls ccs_config/machines/hipergator/

You should see: config_machines.xml, config_batch.xml, gnu_hipergator.cmake

docs.title: Step 5: Customize for Your Group
docs.text:
The HiPerGator batch config names the SLURM QoS queues jobs are submitted to. These must match your group's QoS. Check your group's QoS names and limits:

showQos <group>
showQos <group>-b

Then edit the <queues> block of the batch config to use your QoS names (see CIME Configuration for details):

vim ccs_config/machines/hipergator/config_batch.xml

The jobmax value on each queue is the task count CIME uses to choose a queue. It is not enforced by SLURM, so keep it at or below the QoS cpu limit reported by showQos. The MAX_TASKS_PER_NODE and MAX_MPITASKS_PER_NODE settings in config_machines.xml describe node hardware (128 cores), not QoS, and normally should not be changed.

docs.title: Step 6: Create a Test Case
docs.text:
Test your installation with a simple case:

cd cime/scripts

./create_newcase \
    --case /blue/<group>/$USER/cases/test_case \
    --compset I2000Clm60Sp \
    --res f45_f45_mg37 \
    --machine hipergator \
    --run-unsupported

docs.title: Step 7: Build and Run
docs.text:
cd /blue/<group>/$USER/cases/test_case

# Set up the case
./case.setup

# Build (this takes ~20 minutes the first time)
./case.build

# Submit to the queue
./case.submit

docs.title: Step 8: Check Results
docs.text:
Monitor your job:

squeue -u $USER

Check for output:

# Find your run directory
./xmlquery RUNDIR

# List output files
ls $(./xmlquery --value RUNDIR)/*.nc

docs.title: Fork Modifications
docs.text: This page documents modifications made in our forks and their rationale.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Our forks include HiPerGator-specific changes, bug fixes for building tools, and one research namelist parameter:

Repository Branch Purpose cdevaneprugh/CTSM uf-ctsm5.3.085 Tool fixes, paths, spillheight namelist parameter (retired) cdevaneprugh/ccs_config_cesm uf-hipergator Machine config cdevaneprugh/NCAR-NEON uf-osbs NEON→DATM forcing generator (offline fork; AGPL-3.0)

The first two are CTSM build/machine forks (detailed below). NCAR-NEON is a different kind of fork — the NEON atmospheric-forcing generator (flow.api.clm.R), modified to run fully offline on HiPerGator to produce input data rather than build the model. It is AGPL-3.0 (kept separate from the MIT hpg-esm-tools repository for that reason) and is documented in full, with the edit table, at NEON Atmospheric Forcing.

docs.title: 1. CMakeLists.txt - STATIC vs SHARED
docs.text:
File: tools/mksurfdata_esmf/src/CMakeLists.txt

Problem: Upstream declares libraries as STATIC IMPORTED but points to shared .so files:

# Buggy upstream code
add_library(pioc STATIC IMPORTED)
set_property(TARGET pioc PROPERTY IMPORTED_LOCATION $ENV{PIO}/lib/libpioc.so)

This is an internal inconsistency - you cannot declare STATIC and point to a shared library.

Fix: Change to SHARED IMPORTED:

add_library(pioc SHARED IMPORTED)
add_library(piof SHARED IMPORTED)

Why it works at NCAR: Their systems likely have PIO as static libraries, or use different CMake handling.

Upstream status: Merged as ESCOMP/CTSM #3700 (2026-02-18), first released in ctsm5.4.021.

docs.title: 2. mksurfdata.F90 - Format Specifiers
docs.text:
File: tools/mksurfdata_esmf/src/mksurfdata.F90

Problem: gfortran requires an explicit width in Fortran I edit descriptors. The I format without a width is a legacy extension:

! Buggy - no width specified
write(ndiag,'(2(a,I))') ' npes = ', npes, ' grid size = ', grid_size
read(nfpio, '(i)', iostat=ier) pio_iotype

Fix: Use I0 (minimal width) for the two writes and an explicit width for the read:

write(ndiag,'(2(a,I0))') ' npes = ', npes, ' grid size = ', grid_size              ! line 271
read(nfpio, '(I6)', iostat=ier) pio_iotype                                        ! line 295
write (ndiag,'(a, I0, a, I0)') ' node_count = ', node_count, ' grid_size = ', grid_size  ! line 328

Lines modified: 271 and 328 (writes), 295 (read)

Why it works at NCAR: They likely use Intel compilers, which accept the width-less form.

Upstream status: Merged as ESCOMP/CTSM #3701 (2026-03-12), first released in ctsm5.4.025. The upstream lines are identical to the fork's.

docs.title: 3. gen_mksurfdata_build - GCC Compatibility Flags
docs.text:
File: tools/mksurfdata_esmf/gen_mksurfdata_build

Problem: Since GCC 10, gfortran treats two legacy patterns as hard errors rather than warnings: mismatched argument types between calls to the same procedure (for example MPI calls through mpif.h), and BOZ literal constants used outside DATA statements. CIME case builds already receive the relevant flags from the stock ccs_config/machines/cmake_macros/gnu.cmake (for GCC 10 and later), but mksurfdata has its own CMake build that does not use those macros. HiPerGator builds with GCC 14.2.0.

Fix: Pass the compatibility flags to the mksurfdata CMake configure step (line 170):

-DCMAKE_Fortran_FLAGS=" -fallow-argument-mismatch -fallow-invalid-boz -ffree-line-length-none"

Flags explained: - -fallow-argument-mismatch: Downgrade argument type mismatches from errors to warnings - -fallow-invalid-boz: Downgrade invalid BOZ literal constants from errors to warnings - -ffree-line-length-none: Remove the 132-column free-form line limit

Upstream status: Not upstreamed. These are workarounds, not fixes for the underlying code patterns.

docs.title: 4. single_point_case.py - MPILIB
docs.text:
File: python/ctsm/site_and_regional/single_point_case.py

Change: MPILIB=mpi-serial → MPILIB=openmpi

Reason: HiPerGator uses OpenMPI, not mpi-serial.

Contribution candidate: No - HiPerGator-specific.

docs.title: mpi-serial Incompatibility
docs.text:
Why We Can't Use mpi-serial

This section explains why single-point runs still require OpenMPI, even though CIME supports mpi-serial for truly serial execution.

What is mpi-serial?

mpi-serial is a stub MPI library that provides MPI function signatures without actual parallelization. It's designed for running MPI-dependent code on a single processor without a real MPI installation.

Why we investigated it:

  • Single-point CTSM runs use only 1 MPI task
  • Interactive execution without SLURM would be convenient for testing
  • Simpler build environment (no MPI dependencies)

Why it doesn't work with modern CTSM:

CTSM 5.3+ uses CDEPS (Community Data models for Earth Prediction Systems) for atmospheric data and CMEPS (the NUOPC-based Community Mediator for Earth Prediction Systems) for coupling, replacing the MCT-based data models and CPL7 coupler. CDEPS requires ESMF (Earth System Modeling Framework).

On HiPerGator, ESMF is built with OpenMPI. When you try to build CTSM with MPILIB=mpi-serial:

# Build fails at link stage:
/apps/.../libesmf.a: undefined reference to symbol 'ompi_mpi_unsigned_short'
/apps/.../libmpi.so.40: error adding symbols: DSO missing from command line

The ESMF library contains calls to OpenMPI-specific symbols that mpi-serial doesn't provide.

The workaround:

Single-point runs work fine with OpenMPI using NTASKS=1. You still need to submit jobs via SLURM, but the job runs on a single core. This is how our fork is configured.

Bottom line: If you're coming from an older CTSM version or another machine where mpi-serial worked, be aware it's not an option with modern CTSM on HiPerGator.

docs.title: 5. default_data_*.cfg - Input Paths
docs.text:
Files: tools/site_and_regional/default_data_2000.cfg, default_data_1850.cfg

Change: NCAR paths → HiPerGator paths

Example: 

# Before (NCAR)
[main]
clmforcingindir = /glade/campaign/...

# After (HiPerGator)
[main]
clmforcingindir = /blue/<group>/earth_models/inputdata

docs.title: 6. namelist_definition_ctsm.xml - spillheight (research parameter, retired)
docs.text:
File: bld/namelist_files/namelist_definition_ctsm.xml

Change: A new namelist entry spillheight (type real, group hillslope_properties_inparm, no default in the definition), added 2026-01-12 (commit 4a0319fee):

<entry id="spillheight" type="real" category="physics"
        group="hillslope_properties_inparm">
Height threshold (m) for water to accumulate before draining to stream.
Subtracts from hillslope_elevation to create a bank effect.
</entry>

Reason: Stock CTSM has no such parameter. It exists only in the PI's HillslopeHydrologyMod.F90 SourceMod, which reads it from the hillslope_properties_inparm group and subtracts it from every hillslope column's hill_elev at initialization (default 0.2 m in the SourceMod). The fork entry lets the value be set from user_nl_clm instead of by editing the SourceMod; without it, CTSM's namelist validation rejects the variable. It is only meaningful in a case that also carries that SourceMod.

Status: Retired. The offset was superseded by raw-HAND binning on 2026-04-30 and every production case sets spillheight = 0.0; the PI later removed the parameter from his SourceMods (2026-05-19). The entry is kept so that existing cases' user_nl_clm files remain valid. See SPILLHEIGHT: the retired runtime offset.

Contribution candidate: No - research-specific and retired.

docs.text:

docs.title: Shared PIO Library Support
docs.text:
The fork configures CTSM to use a pre-built PIO library instead of rebuilding it for every case. This is controlled by environment variables in config_machines.xml:

<env name="PIO_VERSION_MAJOR">2</env>
<env name="PIO_TYPENAME_VALID_VALUES">netcdf</env>
<env name="LD_LIBRARY_PATH">/blue/<group>/earth_models/shared/parallelio/bld/lib:$ENV{LD_LIBRARY_PATH}</env>

How CIME decides whether to use external PIO:

if PIO_VERSION_MAJOR is set AND matches case PIO_VERSION:
    → use external PIO from PIO_LIBDIR
    → build log shows "Using installed PIO library"
else:
    → build PIO from source into EXEROOT/shared/pio2
    → adds several minutes to each case.build

Variable purposes:

Variable Purpose PIO_VERSION_MAJOR Triggers external PIO usage (value must match your PIO version) PIO_TYPENAME_VALID_VALUES Specifies I/O backends (our build supports netcdf only) LD_LIBRARY_PATH Required for runtime linking to shared .so files

See CIME Configuration for more details.

docs.title: Why Fork ccs_config?
docs.text:
The ~/.cime/ user override approach has CIME v3 bugs: - Batch config loading inconsistent - NODENAME_REGEX detection issues - Each user must maintain configs

Forking gives a single source of truth.

docs.title: Hillslope Hydrology
docs.text: CTSM's hillslope hydrology mode enables representation of subgrid topography with lateral water flow between landscape positions.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Traditional ESM land models use a 1-D (vertical) hydrology approach - each gridcell is treated as a flat slab with no internal terrain structure. This misses critical landscape processes:

  • Drier hills, wetter valleys
  • Ridge-to-valley groundwater convergence
  • Delayed water delivery (temporal carryover)
  • Aspect-dependent radiation differences

CTSM's hillslope hydrology mode addresses these limitations by dividing each gridcell into multiple columns at different topographic positions connected by lateral water flow.

docs.title: Column Organization
docs.text:
Hillslope mode partitions each gridcell into an arbitrary number of columns at different topographic positions. The cardinality is read at runtime from the hillslope input NetCDF (nhillslope × nmaxhillcol), so the same CTSM build supports varied column-structure decisions.

The Swenson global default uses 4 aspects × 4 elevation bins = 16 columns:

Gridcell (Swenson default)
├── North-facing hillslope (4 columns: Outlet → Lower → Upper → Ridge)
├── East-facing hillslope (4 columns)
├── South-facing hillslope (4 columns)
└── West-facing hillslope (4 columns)

The OSBS production file departs from this default, using 1 aspect × 24 elevation bins + 1 dedicated lake column = 25 columns. The aspect partition is collapsed because OSBS slopes are too shallow (bin means: median ~0.05 m/m, max ~0.07 m/m) for aspect-dependent insolation to carry a meaningful signal; the 24 elevation bins resolve the wet-to-dry gradient at the LIDAR vertical noise floor. See HAND Binning and Lake Column for the OSBS rationale.

Stream channel properties (depth, width, slope) are stored at the hillslope landunit level in either configuration, not as a separate column.

docs.title: Six Geomorphic Parameters
docs.text:
Each hillslope element is defined by six parameters (Swenson & Lawrence 2025):

Parameter Symbol Description Area A Horizontally projected surface area Height h Mean height above stream channel (HAND) Distance d Distance from channel to the element's area midpoint on the fitted trapezoidal plan form (median DTND as fallback) Width w Width at downslope interface Slope α Mean topographic slope Aspect β Azimuthal orientation (from North)

docs.title: HAND and DTND
docs.text:
Two key metrics organize the hillslope:

  • HAND (Height Above Nearest Drainage): Elevation relative to nearest stream pixel
  • DTND (Distance To Nearest Drainage): Horizontal distance to nearest stream pixel

These define the hillslope profile (height vs distance from stream).

docs.title: Three Hillslope-Enabled Processes
docs.text:
1. Lateral subsurface flow: Water moves between columns based on hydraulic gradient using Darcy's Law
  2. Aspect-dependent insolation: Solar radiation varies by slope and aspect
  3. Elevation downscaling: Temperature and precipitation adjusted by elevation

docs.title: Why Darcy's Law Matters
docs.text:
The paper emphasizes using Darcy's Law instead of kinematic wave for lateral flow:

  • Kinematic wave uses constant terrain slope
  • Darcy's Law captures negative feedbacks:
    • High water table → accelerated drainage
    • Low water table → decelerated drainage
  • Preserves deep soil water storage
  • Captures delayed hill-to-valley transfer

docs.title: Two-Way Surface-Groundwater Exchange
docs.text:
Rivers can both gain and lose water:

  • Gaining: Higher water table feeds stream
  • Losing: Stream water infiltrates to groundwater
  • Dynamic connectivity: Channel network expands/contracts with conditions

docs.title: Global Hillslope Dataset (Swenson & Lawrence 2025)
docs.text:
The default global dataset was created from MERIT DEM (~90m resolution):

  • Resolution: ~1° globally
  • Source: MERIT DEM
  • Limitation: Too coarse for low-relief wetlands

The paper explicitly notes:

"The MERIT DEM... may not be fine enough to capture topographic variations in areas of very low topographic relief, such as wetlands."

docs.title: Custom Data for Low-Relief Sites
docs.text:
For sites like OSBS, custom hillslope parameters from high-resolution LIDAR provide:

  • 90x finer resolution than global dataset
  • Capture of wetland basin morphology
  • Identification of actual stream/drainage networks
  • Resolution of TAI transition zones

Workflow for custom data:

  1. Obtain 1m LIDAR DEM (e.g., from NEON)
  2. Apply Laplacian spectral analysis to find characteristic length scale
  3. Use pysheds for catchment delineation
  4. Calculate HAND/DTND at high resolution
  5. Discretize and average to create hillslope parameters
  6. Format for CTSM surface dataset

Tool: Representative_Hillslopes

docs.title: Low-Relief Wetlands
docs.text:
In humid, low-relief regions (like OSBS), lateral drainage matters for different reasons than mountains:

"In humid and low-relief regions where water is in excess, lateral drainage is also important but for different reasons. Here regional drainage is impeded, resulting in waterlogged soils and oxygen stress for plants."

Slightly elevated mounds improve local drainage and alleviate waterlogging, supporting upland vegetation.

docs.title: TAI Dynamics
docs.text:
The Terrestrial-Aquatic Interface (TAI) is the dynamic boundary between wet and dry areas:

  • TAI position shifts with water level changes
  • TAI dynamics drive carbon flux "hot spots" and "hot moments"
  • Hillslope mode can represent these transitions via water table position in different columns

docs.title: Key Namelist Parameters
docs.text: CTSM hillslope mode is controlled by two related-but-distinct toggles. A 2026-05-19 source-code audit of CTSM 5.3.085 established what each one activates; the Lateral Flow and Routing page documents the file:line evidence.

docs.title: use_hillslope
docs.text:
use_hillslope = .true.

Activates inter-column lateral subsurface flow. With this toggle on, PerchedLateralFlow and SubsurfaceLateralFlow (SoilHydrologyMod.F90) are dispatched unconditionally from HydrologyDrainageMod.F90; the Darcy gradient between adjacent columns is computed every hydrology step, and the net inflow/outflow is applied to each column's soil-water state. This is what makes a hillslope-mode case differ physically from a stack of independent 1-D soil columns.

docs.title: use_hillslope_routing
docs.text:
use_hillslope_routing = .false.    ! current OSBS production setting

When set to .true., this additionally activates the stream-side machinery: an internal stream_water_volume ledger, Manning's-equation streamflow at the chain bottom, a stream-channel boundary condition that supersedes MOSART's tdepth_grc at the terminal column, the VOLUMETRIC_STREAMFLOW history field, and the land-to-runoff streamflow export. Routing-on does not activate inter-column lateral flow — that already runs under use_hillslope alone. The operative case osbs.swenson.spinup runs with routing off; see Lateral Flow and Routing for the source-code evidence.

docs.text: Documentation for NEON (National Ecological Observatory Network) site simulations.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
NEON provides standardized, high-quality observational data across 81 field sites in the United States. For CTSM validation, NEON offers:

  • Flux tower data: Carbon, water, and energy fluxes
  • Meteorological forcing: Required for atmospheric data model (DATM)
  • Soil surveys: Profiles, texture, organic carbon
  • Vegetation surveys: Species composition, biomass
  • LIDAR topography: 1m resolution DEMs for many sites

docs.title: CTSM Integration
docs.text:
CTSM includes built-in support for NEON sites:

  • Pre-configured site definitions
  • Automated data download scripts
  • Standardized forcing data processing

See Single-Point Runs for creating site simulations.

docs.title: Why OSBS for Hillslope Research
docs.text:
OSBS represents a low-relief wetlandscape - the exact setting where hillslope hydrology matters most:

  1. Subtle topography: Elevation differences of meters (not hundreds of meters) drive ecosystem patterns
  2. TAI dynamics: Wetland-upland boundaries shift seasonally
  3. Groundwater-driven: Lateral subsurface flow dominates over surface connectivity
  4. High-quality data: Extensive NEON instrumentation and 1m LIDAR

From Fan et al. 2019:

"In humid and low-relief regions where water is in excess, lateral drainage is also important... the slightly elevated hills can improve local drainage and alleviate waterlogging."

OSBS fits "Position 3" in Fan 2019 Figure 6a (ever-wet, low relief) where hillslope representation improves drainage representation on subtle mounds.

Pre-generated subset data (subset_data output; one directory per configuration):

docs.title: Current Data Strategy
docs.text:
The original OSBS hillslope spinup (osbs.swenson.spinup) uses globally-subset CRUNCEPv7 atmospheric forcing and surface data extracted via CTSM's subset_data script (in tools/site_and_regional/). A site-native NEON forcing dataset has since been produced (Phase I): a fork of the NCAR-NEON pipeline, run fully offline on HiPerGator, generates the OSBS tower record as 101 monthly DATM files spanning 2017-02 → 2025-06. It reproduces the pre-built NCAR-NEON v4 product where both carry measured data, has driven a converged AD spinup (osbs.swenson.neon.spinup), and has been handed to the PI for adoption. See NEON Atmospheric Forcing for the full methodology and the dtlimit = -1 requirement for cycled runs.

An earlier report that the pre-built run_tower NEON forcing was "insufficient" was traced to a namelist year-cap, not a data limit — the pre-built product reaches 2024-12. run_tower remains useful for basic NEON site tests, but for OSBS production forcing it is superseded by the offline pipeline above.

docs.title: Custom Hillslope Data for OSBS
docs.text:
The global Swenson hillslope dataset (~90 m source resolution) is too coarse for OSBS. Custom hillslope parameters were generated from 1 m NEON LIDAR (DP3.30024.001) using the Swenson & Lawrence (2025) methodology, resolving:

  • Actual wetland basin morphology
  • Fine-scale drainage network identification
  • TAI transition zone resolution

The finished parameters bear out the contrasts anticipated against the global data: a much smaller characteristic length scale (Lc = 356 m), low HAND values (meters, not tens of meters), and a single-aspect structure rather than four distinct hillslopes. The production file hillslopes_osbs_production_c260505.nc (25 columns: 1 lake + 24 land bins) is deployed in the operative spinup case.

This work is documented in full in the Swenson Implementation section — see Overview, OSBS Hillslope Methodology, and HAND Binning and Lake Column.

docs.title: Research Overview
docs.text: This section documents research applications of CTSM on HiPerGator, focusing on wetlandscape hydrology and carbon dynamics.

docs.title: DOE Project: Water and Carbon Dynamics of Coastal Plain Wetlandscapes
docs.text: Funding: DOE-BER Terrestrial-Aquatic Interfaces program (2023-2026)

docs.title: The Problem
docs.text:
Wetlandscapes are low-relief mosaics of wetlands embedded in terrestrial uplands. The Terrestrial-Aquatic Interface (TAI) - the dynamic boundary between wet and dry areas - drives the bulk of carbon exchange, but current Earth System Models treat wetland extent as static.

Fan et al. (2019) identify these limitations of generic ESM land hydrology (not all apply to CTSM, which already has a prognostic water table, ZWT):

  • 1-D vertical hydrology - no lateral flow between landscape positions
  • 2-3m shallow soil - misses deep moisture storage and Critical Zone processes
  • Free-draining - instant drainage to rivers, no water table dynamics
  • No terrain structure - flat slab with no ridges/valleys

docs.title: Research Goals
docs.text:
The grant's aspirational goals (full wetlandscape simulation) require first solving a fundamental problem: individual wetlands aren't properly represented in ESMs.

Current focus: Improve individual wetland representation in CTSM using hillslope hydrology to capture TAI dynamics.

docs.title: Technical Approach
docs.text:
Using CTSM's hillslope hydrology feature to represent within-gridcell topography:

  • Multiple columns per gridcell at different elevations
  • Lateral water flow between columns
  • Different water table depths affect biogeochemistry
  • Even subtle Florida topography (meters, not hundreds of meters) matters for TAI position

docs.title: Hillslope Hydrology
docs.text:
CTSM's hillslope mode divides gridcells into multiple topographic positions with lateral water flow. This enables representation of:

  • Ridge-to-valley water redistribution
  • Aspect-dependent radiation (N, E, S, W facing slopes)
  • Dynamic water table position
  • Wetland-upland transitions

See Hillslope Hydrology for technical details.

docs.title: NEON Site Simulations
docs.text:
NEON (National Ecological Observatory Network) provides high-quality observational data for model validation:

  • Flux tower measurements (carbon, water, energy)
  • Meteorological forcing data
  • Soil and vegetation surveys
  • High-resolution LIDAR topography

See NEON Sites for site-specific information.

docs.text:
Phase: Analysis and investigation. The 600-yr accelerated AD spinup with the custom OSBS hillslope file completed 2026-05-14 and was analyzed 2026-05-19. The bridge-zone water-table anomaly at flood-zone chain indices 3–6 was resolved by the PI (2026-08-19); the PI continues to investigate the remaining open question — the absence of the anoxia-based TAI signal in decomposition output.

docs.title: Case Workflow
docs.text: CTSM uses a case-based workflow where each simulation is configured, built, and run from a dedicated case directory.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
create_newcase → case.setup → case.build → case.submit

Each step creates or modifies files in the case directory.

docs.title: 1. Create a New Case
docs.text:
cd $CIME_SCRIPTS

./create_newcase \
    --case $CASES/my_case_name \
    --compset I1850Clm60BgcCrop \
    --res f09_g17 \
    --machine hipergator \
    --run-unsupported

Key arguments:

Argument Description --case Path to the case directory --compset Component set (model configuration) --res Resolution (grid) --machine Target machine --run-unsupported Allows a compset/grid combination that CESM has not tested or scientifically supported (needed for CLM_USRDAT single-point grids; unrelated to the machine)

docs.title: 2. Configure the Case
docs.text:
cd $CASES/my_case_name

# Modify XML settings
./xmlchange STOP_OPTION=nyears
./xmlchange STOP_N=5
./xmlchange JOB_WALLCLOCK_TIME=04:00:00

# Query current values
./xmlquery STOP_OPTION STOP_N

Common XML variables:

Variable Description Example STOP_OPTION Time units nyears, nmonths, ndays STOP_N Number of time units 5 JOB_WALLCLOCK_TIME SLURM time limit 04:00:00 NTASKS Number of MPI tasks 32

docs.title: 3. Setup the Case
docs.text:
./case.setup

This creates: - Namelist files (user_nl_clm, etc.) - Build scripts - Run scripts

docs.title: 4. Modify Namelists
docs.text:
Edit user_nl_clm to customize model behavior:

! Example: Configure history output
hist_empty_htapes = .true.
hist_fincl1 = 'TSA', 'GPP', 'EFLX_LH_TOT'
hist_nhtfrq = -24
hist_mfilt = 365

docs.title: 5. Build the Case
docs.text:
./case.build

This compiles the model. Takes 10-30 minutes depending on configuration.

Rebuilding: If you change Fortran source code or XML build variables: 

./case.build --clean-all
./case.build

docs.title: 6. Submit the Case
docs.text:
./case.submit

This submits the job to SLURM. Monitor with: 

squeue -u $USER

docs.title: Directory Structure
docs.text:
After setup, each case has these key directories:

Directory Variable Purpose Case root CASEROOT Configuration, scripts, namelists Build EXEROOT Compiled executables Run RUNDIR Output, restarts, logs Archive DOUT_S_ROOT Archived output

Query paths: 

./xmlquery EXEROOT RUNDIR DOUT_S_ROOT

docs.text:
Compset Description I1850Clm60BgcCrop Pre-industrial BGC with crops I2000Clm60BgcCrop Present-day BGC with crops I1850Clm60Sp Pre-industrial satellite phenology IHistClm60BgcCrop Historical transient run

List available compsets: 

./query_config --compsets clm
